_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, multiple fixed dose, multi-center trial randomizing patients with RRMS to placebo, DMF 240 mg BID, or DMF 240 mg TID over two years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: proportion of patients relapsed at 2 years
pivotal_trials.result: Proportion relapsing: 42% placebo vs 24% (240 BID) vs 23% (240 TID); hazard ratios 0.51 and 0.50, p<0.0001 for both

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral BG00012 in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis

pivotal_trials.design: Design similar to Study 301 but with an additional open-label glatiramer acetate arm; primary outcome was ARR rather than proportion relapsing
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: annualized relapse rate (ARR) at 2 years
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted ARR 0.401 placebo vs 0.224 (240 BID) vs 0.198 (240 TID); rate ratios 0.560 and 0.495, p<0.0001 for both

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety Study of Oral BG00012 With Active Reference in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥10% and ≥2% more than placebo) were flushing (40% vs 6%), abdominal pain (18% vs 10%), diarrhea (14% vs 11%), and nausea (12% vs 9%); TECFIDERA may cause lymphopenia
target_moa: Mechanism of action in MS is not fully known; proposed to involve activation of the nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2 (Nrf2) transcriptional pathway, reducing inflammation and promoting cytoprotection

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile was deemed acceptable

description.text: Safety labeling changes: added hypersensitivity reactions, PML, and lymphopenia warnings (no indication change)
Added vaccine information to Section 12.3 of the labeling

description.text: Labeling-only safety revision to Warnings and Precautions (Lymphopenia) on lymphocyte recovery after discontinuation; no change to indication or population

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for revisions to subsection 5.4 (Warnings and Precautions; Lymphopenia) of the Prescribing Information regarding lymphocyte recovery following discontinuation of Tecfidera.

summary.text: Traditional (full) approval of a new molecular entity based on two randomized placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials (Studies 301 and 302); no advisory committee was convened, and postmarketing requirements including a deferred pediatric trial and a long-term safety observational study were imposed

citations.quote: Dimethyl fumarate (DMF) has not been previously approved and is categorized as a new molecular entity.
109MS301 and 109MS302 were both Phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled trials of 2 years duration.

Your application for Tecfidera (dimethyl fumarate) was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.

2014-6: A large, long-term prospective observational study in ≥5000 adult relapsing MS patients, followed ≥5 years, to determine incidence of serious infections, leiomyomata, malignancies (including renal cell cancers), and serious renal/hepatic events with marketed use

citations.quote: **2014-6** A large, long-term, prospective observational study in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, with the primary objective of determining the nature and incidence of serious infections including opportunistic infections, leiomyomata, malignancies including renal cell cancers, and other serious adverse events including serious renal and hepatic events and other medically significant events occurring with marketed use of Tecfidera (dimethyl fumarate). The study should include characterization of the finding of urinary ketones. A minimum of 5000 multiple sclerosis patients treated with Tecfidera (dimethyl fumarate) should be enrolled and followed for a minimum of 5 years. The final protocol should reflect agency agreement and be submitted prior to starting the study.
